title: Streaming after Instantaneity
content:
Speech at INC Exit Fest, OT 301, Amsterdam, 25th June, 2026.

Online video has become the general condition of social media, a streaming vortex driven by extractivism and behavioural targeting. Reflecting on my experience as a member of CDI-TV,[1] a collective contributing to StreamArtNetwork (SAN), I want to consider this condition from a specific angle, what I am calling poor chroma: the shimmering, unstable borders that appear where chroma-keyed bodies fail to seamlessly converge with the background, where a slight glitched-out halo forms around hair and fingers, the signs of a spill that doesn’t quite wash out. They might seem like minor technical imperfections, but I argue that poor chroma offers one way to understand the stakes of streaming in terms of tactical publishing, strategic power and the logistical operations of streaming infrastructures. Poor chroma can help us understand how liveness, distribution and collectivity are both held together and apart by corporate stacks; in other words, how they are interfaced and, therefore, how the mediation within the vortex becomes conceivable.[2]

THE UNSTABLE OBJECT
